question: Where can I get the list of grid connection requests in the United Kingdom, with project, technology, capacity (MW), connection node, status and date?

answer.summary: NESO publishes GB TEC contracts and a separate Scottish embedded register; SONI publishes Northern Ireland connection agreements and effective applications. Distribution operators publish their own registers. These datasets mix connected and future projects and do not provide a complete list of all UK applications.
main_caveats: TEC is a contract register, not all requests; NESO reports no public demand connection register.
An empty Gate field is not Gate 1 or Gate 2: NESO populates it after an agreement is countersigned.
Effective capacity dates are not application dates; connected MW and cumulative stage MW are different.
NESO warns repeated capacity across stages or technologies can cause duplicates.
Distribution coverage varies: Northern Powergrid ECR omits unaccepted enquiries; SONI omits cluster agreements.
answer.confidence_reason: Both NESO CSVs and SONI workbook were downloaded; a distribution CSV is blocked and full UK coverage remains unchecked.

how_to_use.example_result: 012 NEP Coventry West | NEW ENERGY PARTNERSHIP LIMITED | Berkswell GSP | 92.4 MW | Scoping | 31/10/2034 | PRO-003804 | Gate blank
steps: Download the CSV, read the headers and identify projects by Project Number and case-sensitive Project ID.
Read connected MW, increase/decrease, cumulative MW and effective date separately; distinguish built from scoping rows.
Do not sum cumulative MW across stages or repeated technology rows; inspect each project agreement.
reading_traps: Gate is populated after agreement countersignature; blank is not evidence of Gate 1 or rejection.
Aggregated capacity across stages and technologies may repeat in several rows.
MW Effective From is a capacity effective date, not date of application or proof of physical connection.
Corrections may lag while reform governance is in place.
Signed Gate 1 capacity is indicative and dependent on obtaining Gate 2, according to NESO: https://www.neso.energy/document/383501/download
NESO says it has no public demand connections register. https://www.neso.energy/document/390531/download

NESO has disclosed historic TEC versions via FOI-24-0040(a) (2014–2020) and FOI-24-0031 (2021–2025); the current portal is not a routine historical archive. Older versions may lack Project Number. https://www.neso.energy/document/363736/download

steps: Open Connections Register sheet; inspect the separate section headings and rows.

how_to_use.example_result: Northern Powergrid NPg15-000863 | Maiden Hill Farm BESS | Stella South | 99.4 MW | Accepted To Connect | date_accepted 2024-02-14 | target_energisation_date Data Not Available
steps: For Northern Powergrid query the >=1 MW API; total_count returned 937 and two records were requested.
For 50 kW to <1 MW use the second member API, which returned total_count 1893.
Read accepted and connected MW, grid points, offer acceptance and target energisation dates separately.
reading_traps: Only accepted or connected assets are included in the tested Northern Powergrid data, not every enquiry.
Target energisation may be Data Not Available; the first tested row had no date.
Do not confuse registered MW with export/import limits or sum overlapping NESO and DNO records.
One sample point for Maiden Hill falls plausibly in the named Ryton/Gateshead area; coordinates are not a surveyed boundary.
Other distribution datasets may reject automated requests or require registration.

recipe: Open the SONI workbook and find the Battery Storage - Applications Deemed Effective section.
